doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Dick Hyman and the first recording under his own name
summary: Hyman brought him to an Esoteric date and became his key to New York work.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So how were you able to carve out your own niche in New York City after?
Okay I got a name, it’s the name number one on your list of honorees on the paper you sent me — Dick Hyman.

Dick Hyman and I became friends and he — well that’s how I did my very first recording under my own name. He took me on a date to play behind a singer. I don’t even think I had anything written down. He said well just play it, and then play a solo for eight bars here or something. That was Esoteric Records. They were too. So we did the date and they asked me to do a date under my own name, and that was a ten inch LP in the early ‘50s. But then we became such friends that he had me on his dates and vice versa, and he’s such a talent you know, and such a wonderful person, that that was a turning point as far as I’m concerned, in my getting — opening some doors into the jazz field and the commercial recording studio field and all that.
Yeah, he’s been involved in some very interesting projects.
Yeah. What a talent, jeez, great.
It’s like all he has to do is decide he wants to play some kind of thing and he can do it.
He can do it all. Yeah.
